chunks: And it is narrated from ʿImrān al-Ḥalabī that he said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who forgot to fast the three days that are required of the mutamattiʿ when he cannot find the sacrificial animal, until he returned to his family.
He عليه السلام said: “He should send a sacrificial blood-offering.”

key_terms.الثَّلَاثَةَ الْأَيَّامِ: the three days of fasting required in this ruling
key_terms.الْهَدْيَ: the sacrificial animal offered in hajj

ai.seo_question: What should a mutamattiʿ do if he forgot to fast the three days required when he could not find a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the mutamattiʿ who was required to fast three days in place of the sacrificial animal but forgot until returning home. In that case, the Imam عليه السلام rules that he should send a blood-offering instead. The narration concerns the expiatory rulings connected to hajj tamattuʿ.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3103 - It is narrated from Imran al-Halabi that
Abu Abdullah (as) was asked about a man who forgot to fast the three days required of the Mutamatti' if he could not find a sacrificial animal, until he returned to his family.
Imam (as) said: "He should send a sacrificial animal (as compensation)."
